0.4-preface 0.4-preface

Why MAGE?

MAGE's contribution is not a list of practices.

Where the theory came from

This book began with one hard engineering problem, watched closely over months of building a real production system.

What changed

Large software systems have always exceeded what any one engineer can keep in mind.

Why I built a production system to study this

This book began with DocAble, a production service for remediating inaccessible documents.

Evidence and scope

MAGE rests on two complementary kinds of evidence.

What the method turned out to be

Two theses organize MAGE.

Who this book is for

This book is for software engineers who suspect the ground has moved and want to know where to stand.

Lesson1.3-the-agentic-substrate 1.3-the-agentic-substrate

The substrate is a pairing

The substrate is two parts, not one.

The reasoning horizon

Scale creates a reasoning problem before an agent ever enters the picture.

The horizon is a locality problem

It is tempting to read this as a fact about today's context window, and so as a fact that the next model will erase.

Probabilistic work needs external authority

The second problem is not that agents make mistakes while human programmers do not.

The loop is observable

Lesson1.4-the-new-engineering-problem 1.4-the-new-engineering-problem

The representation problem

A broad reasoner can operate on abstractions, but its active reasoning state is finite and large systems contain far more detail than any one engineering question needs.

The authority problem

Autonomous work can be locally constrained and checked without a comprehensive model, but probabilistic implementation cannot be its own final authority, and richer system-level obligations require semantics the environment must obtain somewhere.

Related, but not the same

The two problems are related but neither is reducible to the other.

The shared machinery beneath the views

Derive and join; do not repeat

A model here is **derived** — from the code, or the code from it — never kept beside the code as a parallel document.

State the derivation direction

A model and the code stay equal by derivation, and derivation runs in one of two directions.

Separate observed fact from authored intent

Repository-graph tools demonstrate the descriptive half of the pattern: parse source into a persistent graph so an agent can traverse dependencies and identities without repeatedly rereading files.

Keep map and territory connected

A model earns trust over a claimed surface only if its elements can be related back to the system they represent.

How a model stays trustworthy

Trust is bounded by the model's declared surface.

An executable model is its schema plus its checked predicates

Operationally, an executable model is its structured schema plus the predicates and derivations machines can consume.

Lesson2.6-modeling-behavior-and-execution 2.6-modeling-behavior-and-execution

Reading behavior formally

The models below share a small formal vocabulary.

A remediation job's lifecycle

(no topic sentence — opens on a non-paragraph block)

Ownership over the lifecycle, a specialization

The state machine says what states a job may occupy.

What must hold across every interleaving

*What runs at once, and what stays true across every schedule?* Concurrency is where a correct-in-isolation design becomes a source of races, deadlocks, and torn writes, and the answer cannot be a thought experiment about interleavings.

Where each part runs

*Where does each part run, and which of those placements is a correctness decision?* A functionally correct system can still be mis-deployed.

Correctness in the graph, resource limits in a profile

The placement models raise one more question — *what resources constrain execution?* — and answering it well turns on a single modeling principle, the most portable idea in this chapter: **correctness dependencies stay in the graph; host-specific resource limits live in a scheduler profile.**

What This Model Leaves Open

The policy models the load-and-cost side of execution, but not request latency, cache-hit ratios, or data-movement cost.

Guidance or authority?

Keep one distinction sharp.

Prefer structural prevention where the action space closes

Prefer structural prevention when the legitimate action space can be closed.

Size the work to the reasoning and the assurance

Not every agent task deserves the full apparatus of governed autonomy.

Lesson4.2-brownfield 4.2-brownfield

Start with what you already have

Survey the estate before designing the replacement.

Reconcile the map, then promote obligations

Begin with audit.

Migrate one bounded surface at a time

The near destination is a **trusted map** over the parts that matter now: important claims have known anchors, important implementation regions have explanatory homes, and agents can navigate the join without rediscovering it.

Introduce new authority safely: Audit → Drain → Promote

A valid future invariant is not always a valid present admission rule.

Measure what the map still cannot explain

Models expose what they contain more readily than what they omit.

Derive, don't copy

Recovering a model is only the first step.

Price the investment

A recurring gap does not automatically deserve machinery.

Lesson4.3-validating-change 4.3-validating-change

Independent evidence

To validate a change is to assemble evidence that bears on its obligations and decide what consequence that evidence should have.

Build the oracle

An **oracle** is whatever supplies the judgment against which the observed result is evaluated.

Generate falsifying evidence

Let the engineering claim choose the search.

Derive the obligation set first

Coverage answers a question about a population.

Did the search cover the claim?

Generative validation adds an honesty question that a small example suite can often avoid: **did the campaign search the semantic region the claim is about?** Code coverage answers where execution went.

Give the verdict the right consequence

Validation may report or gate.

Two boundaries for evidence

Part III gave a placement rule for authority: **evaluate an obligation at the earliest boundary where it becomes legible and enforceable.** That catches a problem close to its cause.

The skill skeleton

Deliver the right context—and measure it

Self-governance: apply the method to the agent's own work

Self-governance packages the method itself: **Modeling and Alignment turned on the agent's own engineering work.** It is not a third activity beside those two, and not a third thesis — it is the discipline of applying both to the work as it is produced.

Self-operate: package the operating discipline

Self-operate packages the previous chapter's lifecycles, recovery paths, runbook step types, and operating heuristics.

Worked examples

The instruction satisfied to the letter

"Done" was a claim

The retry that became a storm

The failures so far were about operating the fleet.

Provenance became a lookup

**Problem.** A corrupted document once took four cross-file hops to trace back to the pass that wrote it.
